title: TOKEN SOURCE
rule: one token source paints the hero specimen and the page around it; flip the specimen's theme and the page follows while the band and the controls stay
description: A cobalt band with the claim the page proves, 'Every colour on this page comes from one token source.', and under it, 24 px clear of the band, the live specimen (invented kit) cropped to its Tokens panel, 1200 × 368. Four notes pass under the pinned plate (805 tokens, 36 components, WCAG 2.1 AA, 20 releases); each draws a hairline to the part it names, and the Alert panel arrives in the plate with the '20 releases' note. A note fades as a whole before it reaches the plate. Then three side-column cards in true order (Read to Feed on the live reader, Bayyinah TV, the care platform), each an 880 × 440 plate and a 280 px column, and a record of ten results.
signature: Gentrit Display (Hubot Sans; its sister face draws the digits) with JetBrains Mono, one cobalt. The page has no palette of its own: ground, ink, muted text, lines and the band read the specimen's core values (stone.0, stone.950, stone.600, stone.200, cobalt.600), and the notes and cards read its roles (card.surface, text.primary, action.primary, action.soft, border.focus), so the claim is literally true. The first note says the hook: 'Light or Dark: this page follows.' Motion: S2, the plate pins while the notes pass; a note that crosses the pin line draws its hairline in 180 ms and rings its part in 120 ms; the previous hairline fades in 120 ms. Hairlines end at parts: 805 tokens at the 'One source' row, 36 components at the button lane, WCAG 2.1 AA at the focus-ring lane, 20 releases at the 'Release 1.2 is scheduled' alert. When a note's part is in another row, the row arrives first: the board moves 280 ms with cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1) (transform only), then the hairline draws. A note fades from 1 to 0 over its last 60 px above the pinned plate's bottom edge (view() timeline, @supports guarded); the pin holds until the note before the last one has gone. Theme flip: the specimen's circular reveal changes the source first; the page follows 200 ms later with a 200 ms colour tween; the care chart and the reader keep their state. S1: three cards oldest first, the covered card scales to 0.96 on a view timeline. Phone: the plate ends after the first lane and scrolls itself to the offset that keeps the named part whole and cuts no row; Read to Feed uses its store screenshot there. Keyboard: 'Work' jumps to the cards with no travel. Reduced motion: the plate does not pin, notes do not fade, rows jump, hairlines appear with no draw, the flip switches state, no stack scale.

chroma.source: chroma.mjs method (decode and threshold unchanged) on loop5/token-source/final/d-top.png, 1440 × 900

holdback: Lowest: original, 7/10. The frame is still a claim on a colour band, a product plate and a sticky card stack; lifting the plate 24 px off the band removes the launch-page overlap, but the layout a visitor names is the same as round 4. What carries the page is the device: the page is painted by its own hero, the claim says so on the first screen, and the token names on the page change when the source flips. Harmony and hooks are 8.5, not 9: the reader plate is a 512 px scene centred on its own ground, so about 180 px of that ground shows at each side of the 880 px plate, and a visitor must still press Dark to see the hook work. Known limits: during the specimen's 560 ms reveal its view-transition layer paints over the current hairline's inner run and ring (they return at the end of the reveal); the pinned window with the Alert panel lasts 64 px of scroll on desktop and 30 px on the phone before the plate leaves with the last note. Slop 0: the plate no longer overlaps the band.
